key_insight: QFIRE is a prompt firewall for healthcare LLMs that goes beyond injection detection by blocking out-of-scope, PHI-risky, and cross-patient requests using positive-security scope rules plus obfuscation-aware scanning.
clinical_relevance: It could reduce unsafe data leakage and inappropriate clinical outputs in autonomous medical workflows, where harmful prompts can look legitimate and evade standard injection detectors.
method: Declared-purpose scope constraints to block out-of-scope model use
Asynchronous detector graph with concurrent, cheapest-first rule checks
De-obfuscation layer that normalizes Base64/hex/ROT13, homoglyphs, leetspeak, and zero-width characters
evidence_signal: On 1,968 public injection/jailbreak prompts, QFIRE reached F1 0.86; on the 2,000-prompt QFIRE-HealthBench, it was evaluated against real garak and Microsoft PyRIT healthcare payloads.
watch_item: Performance depends on correctly defining the allowed scope and maintaining rules, so overly broad or poorly tuned policies could still miss novel attacks or create false blocks.
paper_title: Beyond Injection Detection: A Positive-Security Prompt Firewall that Closes the Scope and PHI Gap SOTA Classifiers Miss in Healthcare
